import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert date and time to datetime
coffee_sales['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'] + ' ' + coffee_sales['time'])

# Group by product and customer age group to get total sales
sales_summary = coffee_sales.groupby(['product', 'customer_age_group'])['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Set the figure size
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

# Create a bar plot
sns.barplot(data=sales_summary, x='product', y='total', hue='customer_age_group')

# Add labels and title
plt.title('Total Sales by Product and Customer Age Group', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Product', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=14)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.legend(title='Customer Age Group')

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert date and time to datetime
coffee_sales['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'] + ' ' + coffee_sales['time'])

# Group by product and customer age group to get total sales
sales_summary = coffee_sales.groupby(['product', 'customer_age_group'])['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Set the figure size
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

# Create a bar plot
sns.barplot(data=sales_summary, x='product', y='total', hue='customer_age_group')

# Add labels and title
plt.title('Total Sales by Product and Customer Age Group', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Product', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=14)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.legend(title='Customer Age Group')

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
